title: Hot Lips Page trio records and "Evil Man's Blues"
summary: Bunn recorded the Hot Lips Page trio with Wellman Braud and sang the vocal; he never interfered with other people's sessions.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Uh-huh. I was listening the other day on the tape to the Hot Lips Page --
I know. Yeah, I was listening. Those were really fine records, particularly -- well, "Evil Man's Blues," where you --
Yeah. I sang in that, didn't I?
That's a really nice piece of work. What do you remember about him?
Oh, I know he could blow that horn. That's all I remember. And he was a nice person. He ain't living, is he?
Oh, I don't think so. We were just listening to the Hot Lips Page Trio, "Just Another Woman," is the tune.
That was what, you and Hot Lips and who do you think the bass player was? (Ernest Hill - ed.)
Uh-huh. The intro and everything on the guitar, it sounds almost like an electric guitar. It was a real sharp quality. I don't mean sharp pitch-wise, but I mean kind of piercing.
No, it wasn't no electric guitar.
It sounded different than some of the -- maybe it was the microphone that you used.
Yeah. Any thoughts about that particular tune?
Not really, no. It sounded all right to me as long as I was making that money.
I was going to go on and play another --

The thing with me, I never interfered with nobody's sessions. When they hired me to do my set, you know, do my thing, I done it. [Went through the date with no argument.] I just went and done it. Got paid for it and, "Bye." I mean, that's the only way to be. After I was finished, there's no use me going around there trying to goof.
I imagine that's why everybody's taking me to be, you know, respectable. Because I have been all my life.
Do you remember Hot Lips Page at all?
Where was he from? Do you know?
No, I didn't know where Hot Lips he was from; unless I guess he was from down south somewhere.
Yeah. You met him in New York.
Yeah, I met him in New York.
